issues_detected.description: Seven of the ten file collections are typed collection_type: processed_data, but no preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools or imputation_protocols are present. A reader cannot tell how raw AP-MS, SEC-MS or perturb-seq output became the distributed processed archives.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add preprocessing_strategies and cleaning_strategies entries describing the per-modality pipelines (spectral search and quantification for MS, alignment and guide assignment for perturb-seq, image QC for IF) that produced the archives marked processed_data.

issues_detected.description: No software is named as having produced or transformed the data actually distributed. The tools the record does name fall outside that role: the Cell Mapping Toolkit / MuSIC pipeline is stated by the record itself to produce computed cell maps that 'are not included in this release'; FAIRSCAPE is packaging and provenance-metadata software; NDEx and the UVA Dataverse are sharing and hosting platforms; the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit is acquisition instrumentation.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the processing software and versions that produced each released archive (for example the MS search/quantification engine, CellRanger or equivalent for the perturb-seq reads, and the image processing toolchain), with repository or DOI links.

issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata is provided for any subset; the variables slot is entirely absent, so column, channel and measurement semantics inside the ZIP archives are undocumented.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add variables entries (or per-collection data dictionaries) describing at minimum the MS elution-profile table columns, the perturb-seq atlas matrix fields, and the IF image channel-to-target mapping.

issues_detected.description: distribution_formats declares only the container: format ZIP with media_type application/zip. The scientific payload formats inside the archives (image format for the 12.6 GB of IF data, mass-spectrometry table or mzML-family format, perturb-seq matrix format) and character encoding are never stated, which limits interoperability and harmonization.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the internal file formats and encodings per file collection in addition to the ZIP container, for example OME-TIFF for imaging and TSV/UTF-8 for the elution profile tables.

issues_detected.description: No instance or sample counts are reported at release level: instances lists four instance types with no counts, and source_caveats explicitly declines to assert the project-level totals (1,374 interactions, 53,788 images, 11,739 genes) as release totals. total_file_count: 10 counts archives, not samples.
issues_detected.recommendation: State per-modality counts for this release (images, proteins/baits, guides and cells, elution fractions), even as approximate figures derived from the deposited archives.

issues_detected.description: No change log or errata for this release: errata is absent and updates carries only a forward-looking cadence ('quarterly ... through the end of the project in November 2026'). What changed relative to the October 2025 release can only be inferred from related_datasets notes.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add an errata or release-notes entry stating the delta for V2.0 (notably the addition of AP-MS data for paclitaxel- and vorinostat-treated MDA-MB-468 and the July 15 2026 addition of the three IF image archives).

issues_detected.description: No data anomalies, outliers, batch effects or missing-data documentation are recorded: anomalies and missing_data_documentation are both absent, even though the release spans four assay modalities with partially overlapping protein coverage.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document known quality issues per modality (failed baits, low-confidence guides, out-of-focus or discarded images) and how missingness across the incompletely overlapping protein sets should be handled.

issues_detected.description: The only access URL given is a truncated Dataverse API root, https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/, with no datafile identifier appended, so it does not resolve to any downloadable object; the dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url with the DOI-resolved dataset landing page and give per-collection access URLs including the datafile identifiers.

issues_detected.description: The conforms_to RO-Crate claim is, by the record's own admission, carried from the tier-3 preprint and the March/June 2025 releases: 'the June 2026 release page does not itself restate the packaging format, and its file listing names only cm4ai_release_metadata.zip without stating its internal format.' The conformance assertion is therefore unverified for the version being described.
issues_detected.recommendation: Confirm and state the packaging format of cm4ai_release_metadata.zip for V2.0, or scope the RO-Crate claim to the releases in which it was asserted.

issues_detected.description: Inherited date anomalies are disclosed but unresolved: the release page's Dataset Description block is dated 2025-06-30 on a release published 2026-06-17, and created_on 2025-02-27 is 'reused verbatim from earlier releases'. Top-level ordering (created_on 2025-02-27 < issued 2026-06-17 < last_updated_on 2026-07-15) is itself consistent.
issues_detected.recommendation: Correct or annotate the creation date so it reflects this release's data generation window rather than the collection's first deposit.

issues_detected.description: The KOLF2.1J line is described as 'derived from a healthy male Northern European donor' available via HipSci, i.e. donor-derived human material, while human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is false. The determination is defensible for an established, distributed line, but the consent and ethical provenance of the originating donation are not referenced.
issues_detected.recommendation: Cite the HipSci/ATCC consent and ethical-sourcing provenance for the originating cell lines to close the chain of custody, without changing the human-subjects determination.

issues_detected.description: Regulatory metadata is thin on the classification axis: confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant and other_compliance are unpopulated; regulatory_restrictions records only 'FDA Regulated: No; no export control or regulatory restriction is stated'. Anticipated downstream social impacts (future_use_impacts) are likewise absent despite a substantial ethics programme.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add an explicit confidentiality classification (public/open for this CC BY-NC-SA release) and a future_use_impacts entry capturing the Ethics Module's anticipated social impacts of AI-ready cell maps.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C is well formed and its prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Libraries (LibraData/Dataverse) registrant, which matches the declared publisher https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/ and the citation's 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2' — identifier, publisher and citation agree.

Grant number 1OT2OD032742-01 parses correctly as an NIH award (application type 1, activity code OT2, awarding institute OD, serial 032742, support year -01) and is the known Bridge2AI CM4AI Data Generation Project award; the secondary award 5U54HG012513-02 (Bridge2AI Bridge Center) is also well formed.

The human-subjects determination is internally coherent across independent slots: description and keywords name only cell lines (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J), collection_mechanisms describe instruments rather than recruitment, direct_collection.is_direct is false with an explanation, and sensitive_elements, is_deidentified and human_subject_research all agree. The explicit false flags are substantive documentation, not empty fields.

License semantics are consistently propagated: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 in license_and_use_terms, data_use_permission: no_commercial_use, a prohibited_uses entry whose prohibition_reason cites the non-commercial term, and ip_restrictions naming the Regents of the University of California and Stanford as copyright holders with a Data Access Committee supervising dual licensing.

Subset-to-file-collection cross-references resolve: each of the nine subsets names the archive that carries it, and each of the ten file_collections gives an MD5 checksum, publication date and size, with total_file_count: 10 matching the listed collections.

source_caveats is an unusually disciplined provenance statement: it distinguishes release-level facts from project-level totals, refuses to assert cumulative counts as release counts, and flags the carried-forward conformance claim and the reused creation date — self-disclosure that makes the record's limits auditable rather than hidden.

The version chain is coherent: version 2.0 with version_access listing March 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX), June 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R) and October 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM), each also carried in related_datasets with relationship_type is_new_version_of, and latest_version_doi matching the record's own DOI.

The embargo is reported consistently in two places: known_limitations flags a temporary pre-publication embargo, and raw_data_sources marks exactly the two perturb-seq sources as 'Embargoed' while the MassIVE and Figshare deposits are marked available.

Creator identification is strong for a 46-author release: 40 carry ORCID iRIs, affiliations are given for all, the PI is structurally distinguished with email, and locally minted doi:...#person- identifiers are used transparently where no ORCID was available.

is_tabular: false is semantically appropriate for a release of confocal images, mass-spectrometry elution profiles and single-cell sequencing archives, and the nine subsets each carry explicit is_subpopulation: true / is_data_split: false flags rather than leaving the roles implicit.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: A single persistent identifier is used consistently as the record id, the DOI and the latest-version pointer, and is echoed in the citation string.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Format matches 10.XXXXX/suffix. Prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Libraries Dataverse (LibraData) registrant, consistent with publisher https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/. No RRID is claimed, so no RRID pattern check applies.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description (~1,300 chars) enumerates perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS and immunofluorescence content by cell line and treatment condition and states the overarching objective of delivering 'machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data'.
sub_elements.quality_note: Well beyond the 200-character bar: the description is modality-by-modality specific about what is and is not in this Beta release, naming MDA-MB-468 with paclitaxel/vorinostat and KOLF2.1J iPSCs with NPC, neuron and cardiomyocyte derivatives.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Title, description and keywords are mutually consistent; the description's claims about modality coverage match the subsets and file_collections listings.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 28 terms including AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, CRISPR/Cas9, MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, iPSC, cardiomyocyte, paclitaxel, vorinostat, protein-protein interaction, subcellular imaging, Bridge2AI, CM4AI
sub_elements.quality_note: Far exceeds the five-keyword bar and spans four distinct axes: assay technology, cell line and cell type, perturbagen, and programme affiliation. Synonym pairs (scRNAseq/single-cell RNA sequencing, NPC/neural progenitor cell) aid retrieval.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Every keyword is corroborated somewhere in the body of the record; none are aspirational or off-topic. Programme context (Bridge2AI, CM4AI) is asserted by quoted keyword values, not inferred externally.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://cm4ai.org/; publisher: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/; file_collections: ten named archives with MD5, size and publication date; subsets: nine subsets each cross-referencing its archive
sub_elements.quality_note: A project landing page plus a repository publisher URL, backed by a genuinely hierarchical internal structure — dataset to nine subsets to ten file collections — rather than a bare link.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Both URLs are well formed and plausible for the named organisations; the subset-to-collection references resolve within the document.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven entries with relationship_type values is_new_version_of (x4: K7TGEM, F3TD5R, B35XWX, DXWOS5), is_described_by (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), is_referenced_by (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734), references (doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3)
sub_elements.quality_note: The lineage of this release within the UVA Dataverse collection is fully typed, and each entry carries a note explaining what the target contained and how it differs, e.g. that the October 2025 release 'did not include AP-MS data'.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: parent_datasets is unpopulated, but the predecessor chain is expressed through typed is_new_version_of relationships, which serves the sub-element's purpose. All target DOIs are well formed (10.18130, 10.1101, 10.1038 prefixes all plausible).

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 statement of share/adapt rights and attribution, non-commercial and share-alike conditions; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use. ip_restrictions: 'Copyright for CM4AI data is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise noted; raw image data for spatial proteomics is copyright by The Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University ... commercial use requires a separate license negotiation'.
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the licence and the ownership structure are stated, including the split copyright between UC and Stanford for the imaging data and the existence of a Data Access Committee supervising dual licensing — actionable for anyone assessing reuse or commercial licensing.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The licence, the prohibited_uses commercial entry, the data_use_permission enum and the ip_restrictions commercial-licence clause are mutually consistent; no contradiction between openness claims and restriction claims.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'The release records FDA Regulated: No; no export control or regulatory restriction is stated for the release.' data_governance.committee_contact: Jillian Parker, ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486, jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu; data_governance.access_review_process: 'A Data Access Committee supervises ethical matters related to dataset distribution and potential dual licensing for commercial use.'
sub_elements.quality_note: The regulatory determination is explicit rather than silently omitted, and the governance contact required by this sub-element's full scope is present with ORCID and institutional email, alongside a described access-review process and named stewardship roles.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant and other_compliance are unpopulated (recorded as a low-severity completeness issue). The explicit 'FDA Regulated: No' is treated as meaningful documentation rather than as an empty field, consistent with the instruction that explicit false flags are not to be scored as missing.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats.access_urls: ['https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/']; distribution_formats.notes: 'All ten files in the release are distributed as ZIP archives via the University of Virginia Dataverse. Files above the 1.9 GB browser download limit are obtained through the Data Access API.'; publisher: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: Scored on the 'platform access instructions' limb of this sub-element: the resolvable DOI, the named repository and the specific operational instruction about the 1.9 GB browser limit together tell a user how to retrieve all ten archives, including the three multi-gigabyte image files.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated and the access_urls entry is a bare API root with no datafile identifier appended, so it resolves to nothing on its own — flagged as a low-severity correctness issue. The point is earned on the instructions plus resolvable DOI, not on that URL.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip. file_collections: ten entries each with compression: zip, collection_type (raw_data / processed_data / metadata), MD5 checksum and size, e.g. cm4ai_ifimages_MDA-MB-468_untreated.zip, MD5 6d066e6b9d762284c6aa5d0b44565568, 4.6 GB.
sub_elements.quality_note: A format and a correct MIME type are specified and are carried down to every distributed object with checksums and sizes, which is enough for a user to plan retrieval and verify integrity.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: application/zip is the correct IANA media type for the declared format, and all ten MD5 values are well-formed 32-character hex. The container-only nature of the declaration — no internal payload format or encoding — is a genuine interoperability gap and is charged against Element 3 sub-element 2 rather than twice here.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven typed entries; external_resources: seven entries covering cm4ai.org, the MassIVE Repository, Figshare, NDEx, the Cell Mapping Toolkit at https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with docs at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, FAIRSCAPE at https://fairscape.github.io, and IMP at http://integrativemodeling.org
sub_elements.quality_note: External links are specific and purposeful — each states what the resource holds or does (MassIVE for the MS raw files, Figshare for the CRISPRi atlas, NDEx for map visualisation) rather than listing bare URLs.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All URLs are structurally valid with plausible domains. The MassIVE and Figshare pointers are corroborated by matching raw_data_sources.access_details entries.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on non-E3 evidence: distribution_formats is populated, ten file collections are published with MD5s and sizes, publisher is a public Dataverse instance, and the licence explicitly permits share and adapt.
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Users are free to share ... and adapt ... under the conditions that appropriate credit is given ...; that the material is not used for commercial purposes; and that contributions built upon the material are distributed under the same license'
sub_elements.quality_note: A named, standard, machine-recognisable licence with its permissions and all three conditions spelled out, plus the explicit statement that no additional legal or technological restrictions may be applied.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Reuse is permitted in substance, not merely nominally; the non-commercial limit is consistently reflected in data_use_permission and prohibited_uses.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (distribution_formats populated; ten archives published via UVA Dataverse).
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip; file_collections: compression: zip on all ten entries. No file_collections.resources entries, no internal format, no encoding anywhere in the record.
sub_elements.quality_note: Only the container is declared. For a release of confocal images, mass-spectrometry elution profiles and single-cell matrices, 'ZIP' tells a prospective integrator nothing about whether the payload is OME-TIFF or PNG, mzML or a vendor format, h5ad or MTX — so the information needed to harmonize these data with others is absent.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Distinct from Element 2 sub-element 4, which credits that a format and MIME type are stated at all. This sub-element asks whether formats are standardized for reuse and integration; a container plus no encoding does not answer it, and no schema-level file description compensates.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (published archives, permissive licence).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: 'RO-Crate. The CM4AI preprint and the March 2025 and June 2025 Dataverse releases state that CM4AI output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework ...'; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset. instances additionally carry ontology-coded data_substrate (B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19/58/59/64) and data_topic (B2AI_TOPIC:15/26/34) values.
sub_elements.quality_note: A recognised packaging standard is named and coupled to the FAIRSCAPE framework, and the instance-level Bridge2AI substrate and topic codes give machine-actionable ontology conformance beyond the packaging claim.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The record honestly scopes its own RO-Crate claim, noting the June 2026 release page does not restate it — transparent, but it leaves the assertion unverified for this version (low-severity consistency issue). conforms_to_schema describes the datasheet, not the data payload.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met (published archives, permissive licence), so variable documentation is expected for reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: The variables slot is absent from the record. The closest content is instances entries carrying instance_type, data_substrate and data_topic codes, and subsets descriptions naming the archive each occupies — neither defines variables or their identifiers.
sub_elements.quality_note: No data dictionary, column definition, channel key or measurement-unit documentation exists at any level. A reuser opening cm4ai_mass-spec_MDA-MB-468.zip or the perturb-seq atlas has no documented description of the fields inside.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The absence is not excused by is_tabular: false — the MS elution profiles and perturb-seq atlas are tabular products within a non-tabular release, and the IF images have a documented four-channel structure in instances.notes that is never formalised as variable metadata.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: four use_category entries with examples (AI-ready data for functional genomics research; AI model training; cellular process analysis; analysis of cell architecture under perturbation). prohibited_uses: two entries — clinical decision-making/patient care 'without appropriate regulatory oversight and approval', and commercial use, each with a prohibition_reason.
sub_elements.quality_note: Both limbs are populated and the prohibitions carry reasons rather than bare bans, tying the clinical prohibition to the absence of regulatory oversight and the commercial prohibition to the licence and copyright position.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Prohibitions are semantically consistent with the CC BY-NC-SA licence and with the non-clinical, cell-line provenance of the data. discouraged_uses is absent but the sub-element is satisfied by the two populated limbs.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition fails on external evidence: E1 description and keywords name only cell lines (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J iPSCs) and no participants or patients, and E8 collection_mechanisms describe AP-MS, SEC-MS, confocal imaging and CRISPRi screens rather than recruitment. The governance disjunct is treated as satisfied on the borderline rule: E2's regulatory_restrictions records only that no restriction applies (per #1060 not itself a constraint), but the E2-scope ip_restrictions states an operative distribution constraint — 'a Data Access Committee supervises ethical matters related to dataset distribution and potential dual licensing' — over donor-derived material (KOLF2.1J from a human donor via HipSci). Borderline, so scored rather than excluded.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries. (1) 'Ethical Review for the release is carried out by Vardit Ravitsky (ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca)', with contact_person carrying ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801. (2) 'The Ethics Module employs a methodology inspired by Value-Sensitive Design (VSD) ... including the construction of an axiological repository to guide the articulation of design standards'. Supported by data_governance.access_review_process and committee_contact (Jillian Parker, jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu).
sub_elements.quality_note: Named, contactable ethics reviewers with ORCIDs and institutional emails, a described review methodology, and a governance committee with an access-review process — substantially more than a bare assertion that review occurred.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: No IRB number is present, which is semantically appropriate rather than a gap: with involves_human_subjects false and no participant recruitment, IRB approval would not be expected. data_protection_impacts is absent, consistent with the absence of personal data. No inconsistency is created by the false human-subjects flag.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same determination as sub-element 1: human-subjects condition fails on E1/E8 evidence, governance disjunct taken as satisfied on the borderline rule given the Data Access Committee constraint in E2-scope ip_restrictions and the donor-derived origin of the KOLF2.1J line.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'The release records De-identified Samples: Yes. CM4AI data are described as non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.' Corroborated by direct_collection: 'commercially available, ethically sourced human cell lines ... MDA-MB-468 ... available from ATCC; the KOLF2.1J iPSC line was derived from a healthy male Northern European donor and is available from the ... HipSci resource.'
sub_elements.quality_note: States the deidentification status, the basis for it (tissue-culture provenance, unlinkability with current knowledge), and the sourcing of both lines. The 'with current knowledge' qualifier is an honest acknowledgement that genomic material is not unconditionally unlinkable.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: No formal method such as HIPAA Safe Harbor or k-anonymity is named, and none is expected for established cell lines rather than record-level human data — the described basis is appropriate to the data type. Consistent with sensitive_elements (false, with rationale) and human_subject_research. A residual gap, flagged as low severity, is that the consent provenance of the originating KOLF2.1J donation is not cited.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant condition fails on external evidence: E1 description and keywords reference only cell lines and assays, with no participants, patients or clinical research; E8 collection_mechanisms and acquisition_methods describe mass spectrometry, confocal microscopy and CRISPRi screens with no human recruitment; direct_collection.is_direct is false with the explanation that data were 'generated from commercially available, ethically sourced human cell lines rather than collected directly from individuals'. Per #1060 the governance disjunct does not reach sub-elements 3 to 5, so the Data Access Committee does not make this applicable.
sub_elements.evidence: No participants exist in this release; participant_privacy and reidentification_risk are consequently absent. The exclusion rests on E1, E8 and direct_collection evidence, not on the emptiness of this sub-element's own fields.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. Scoring participant privacy protections against a cell-line release would measure the dataset's subject matter rather than the quality of its documentation.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant condition fails on the same external evidence: E1 names cell lines only; E8 describes instrumentation rather than recruitment; direct_collection states data were not collected from individuals. The governance disjunct does not extend to this sub-element (#1060).
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent is absent, and no consent process from participants could apply — the material is commercially distributed MDA-MB-468 and HipSci KOLF2.1J lines.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator. The separate observation that the originating KOLF2.1J donor's consent provenance is not cited is recorded as a low-severity semantic issue rather than scored here.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Participant condition fails on the same external evidence from E1, E8 and direct_collection; there are no enrolled participants, hence no at-risk population protections or compensation arrangements to document. The governance disjunct does not extend to this sub-element (#1060).
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations and participant_compensation are absent, which is the expected state for a release derived entirely from established cell lines.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present: true; identification: 'Cell type and treatment condition. The release spans MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells under untreated, paclitaxel-treated, and vorinostat-treated conditions; undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J iPSCs; and iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells (NPCs), neurons, and cardiomyocytes.'; distribution: modality-by-modality coverage statement. subsets: nine entries each with is_subpopulation: true.
sub_elements.quality_note: The population structure is expressed on the axis that matters for this data type — cell line by differentiation state by perturbagen — and the distribution field is explicit that coverage is uneven across modalities (AP-MS treated only; IF MDA-MB-468 only), which is precisely the kind of actionable detail a reuser needs.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The subpopulation description agrees with the description field, the subsets list and the file_collections inventory; no modality is claimed in one place and missing in another.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met.
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: seven entries, each with an explicit relationship_type — is_new_version_of (K7TGEM, F3TD5R, B35XWX, DXWOS5), is_described_by (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), is_referenced_by (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734), references (doi:10.1038/s41586-025-08878-3, with NDEx uuid f693137a-d2d7-11ef-8e41-005056ae3c32, MassIVE MSV000097168 and ProteomeXchange PXD052362).
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationships are typed with standard vocabulary terms and each carries a note explaining the target and why it relates, including a careful distinction that the Nature U2OS cell map is 'a distinct dataset' by overlapping investigators rather than part of this release.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship directions are used correctly (is_described_by for the describing preprint, references for the independent U2OS study), and every target identifier is a well-formed DOI. The version chain is consistent with version_access.

strengths: Identification and citation are exemplary: a well-formed UVA Dataverse DOI used consistently as id, doi, latest_version_doi and within a complete 46-author citation string, backed by 40 ORCID-identified creators, ROR institutional identifiers, an identified PI and point of contact, and named maintainers with working emails.

The release lineage is fully traceable — version 2.0 with every predecessor individually citable by DOI in version_access and mirrored as typed is_new_version_of relationships, plus a quarterly update cadence and an institutionally funded long-term preservation commitment.

Collection and acquisition are documented at protocol depth across all four modalities: IF stain-to-channel assignments, six guide RNAs per gene with inducible dCas9 and 10x 3'HT readout, and the explicit rationale for using AP-MS and SEC-MS as orthogonal approaches.

Ethical and governance documentation is strong and internally coherent for a cell-line release: named ethics reviewers with contacts, a Data Access Committee with a described access-review process, a Value-Sensitive Design methodology, and explicit negative determinations on human subjects, sensitivity and FDA regulation that state their reasoning rather than leaving fields blank.

Unusual provenance discipline: source_caveats separates release-level facts from project-level totals, refuses to reattribute cumulative counts to this release, and flags its own carried-forward RO-Crate claim and reused creation date — making the record's limits auditable instead of concealed.
Distribution integrity is verifiable per object, with MD5 checksums, sizes and publication dates for all ten archives, and subset-to-archive cross-references that resolve.
Limitations are candid and consequential, including the headline warning that the project's integrated cell maps are not in this release and a statement of what the release is therefore suitable for.
weaknesses: Nothing is documented about how the released data were produced from raw instrument output: preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are all absent, while seven archives are typed processed_data.

No software that produced or transformed the distributed data is named; the tools that are named are a pipeline whose outputs the record says are absent from this release (Cell Mapping Toolkit / MuSIC), packaging and metadata software (FAIRSCAPE), hosting and visualisation platforms (Dataverse, NDEx, Cytoscape), and capture instrumentation (10x 3'HT kit).
No variable-level metadata or data dictionary exists at any level, so the contents of the MS tables, the perturb-seq matrices and the IF image channels are undocumented for a reuser.

Formats are declared only as the ZIP container with media_type application/zip; internal payload formats and character encoding are never stated, which blocks harmonization with other proteomics or imaging collections.
No instance or sample counts are reported for the release — no image, protein, bait, guide or cell counts — so the scale of each modality can only be inferred from archive sizes.
No data quality reporting: anomalies and missing_data_documentation are both absent for a release spanning three assay families with well-known failure modes.

No change log or errata for V2.0; the updates block states only a future quarterly cadence, leaving the delta from the October 2025 release (notably the new AP-MS data) inferable only from related_datasets notes.
Regulatory metadata lacks a confidentiality classification, and future_use_impacts is absent so anticipated downstream social impacts are never analysed despite an active ethics programme.
recommendations: Add per-modality preprocessing_strategies and cleaning_strategies with used_software naming the actual tools and versions that produced the distributed archives (MS search and quantification engine, read alignment and guide assignment for perturb-seq, image QC and processing), each with a repository or software DOI.

Publish per-collection data dictionaries as variables entries: elution-profile table columns with units, perturb-seq atlas matrix fields, and the IF image channel-to-target mapping already described in prose in instances.notes.

Record the internal file formats and encodings inside each ZIP (for example OME-TIFF for imaging, an open MS format for the proteomics tables, an open matrix format for the atlas) alongside the container declaration.
Report release-level counts for each modality — images, proteins and baits, guides and cells, elution fractions — so the release's scale is stated rather than inferred from archive sizes.
Populate anomalies and missing_data_documentation with per-modality quality issues, QC thresholds and discarded-data criteria, and state explicitly whether imputation was used.
Add an errata or release-notes entry describing what changed in V2.0, including the addition of AP-MS data and the later 2026-07-15 deposit of the three immunofluorescence archives.
Populate download_url with the DOI-resolved landing page and give per-collection access URLs that include datafile identifiers, rather than the bare API root currently in access_urls.

Add a confidentiality_level classification and a future_use_impacts entry capturing the Ethics Module's anticipated social impacts, and cite the HipSci/ATCC consent and ethical-sourcing provenance for the originating cell lines.
